nodes.label: Setup notification button
nodes.detail: "Setup Notification" under Settings > Notifications. Pressing it opens NotificationDialog with no argument, i.e. in create mode.

nodes.label: Edit link for a notification target
nodes.detail: Edit on each row of the list. Passes notification.id and opens NotificationDialog in edit mode.

nodes.label: Open the notification dialog
nodes.detail: With an ID it JSON.parses the config from $root.notificationList and restores it. Without one, it is an empty form with type=telegram.

nodes.label: Notification type select
nodes.detail: Nine optgroup categories. Choosing one swaps currentForm and renders the form for that type.

nodes.label: Save button
nodes.detail: type=submit, reached through the form's @submit.prevent="submit". Disabled while processing.

nodes.label: Test button
nodes.detail: Sends a test with the values currently in the form, without saving. It works even while creating a new one.

nodes.label: Delete button
nodes.detail: v-if="id", so it only shows in edit mode. Pressing it closes the modal and opens the confirm dialog.

nodes.label: Delete confirm dialog
nodes.detail: The Confirm component. @yes calls deleteNotification. No does nothing.

nodes.label: Default enabled switch
nodes.detail: isDefault. It only pre-checks the box on the new-monitor screen; existing monitors are untouched.

nodes.label: Apply to all existing monitors
nodes.detail: applyExisting. Links the notification to every monitor once, at save time. A transient flag that is never stored in the DB.

nodes.label: Apprise install status
nodes.detail: If appriseInstalled is true it says installed; if false it shows a link explaining how to install it.

nodes.label: Notification target checkbox
nodes.detail: Puts true/false into monitor.notificationIDList[id]. One checkbox per notification target.

nodes.label: Add a notification from the monitor form
nodes.detail: Opens the same NotificationDialog from the monitor edit screen. Whatever you add gets checked automatically.

nodes.label: Resend count setting
nodes.detail: resendInterval. How many beats it stays DOWN before resending. 0 means never resend.

nodes.label: Monitor save button
nodes.detail: id=monitor-submit-btn. type=submit calls submit(). Disabled while processing.

nodes.label: Save the notification target
nodes.detail: Emits addNotification. On ok it closes and shows a toast. Only a new one emits the added event to the parent.

nodes.label: Send a test
nodes.detail: Sends the unsaved notification object straight through testNotification. The result is only a toast.

nodes.label: Delete the notification target
nodes.detail: Emits deleteNotification with this.id. On ok the modal closes.

nodes.label: Show the delete confirmation
nodes.detail: Hides the settings modal first, then shows Confirm. That order avoids stacked modals.

nodes.label: Auto-number the default name
nodes.detail: Counts up in "Type 1" form until the name does not clash with an existing one. It only overwrites an empty name or an untouched old default name.

nodes.label: Receive the notification list
nodes.detail: Replaces $root.notificationList wholesale with the notificationList from the server.

nodes.label: Add a monitor
nodes.detail: socket.emit("add", monitor, callback). The monitor carries notificationIDList.

nodes.label: Save the monitor
nodes.detail: New and clone emit $root.add; edit emits editMonitor. The low-interval confirmation and the input validation come first.

nodes.label: Auto-enable the notification just added
nodes.detail: Takes the dialog's added event and sets the new ID to true in notificationIDList. It never fires while editing.

nodes.label: Pre-check the default notification targets
nodes.detail: Only when creating: every notification target with isDefault true is put into notificationIDList automatically.

nodes.label: Ask whether Apprise is installed
nodes.detail: The Apprise form's mounted emits checkApprise and stores the answer in appriseInstalled.

nodes.label: socket.io connection accepted
nodes.detail: Every UI-initiated action passes through here. Right after connecting it returns sendInfo, then registers the event handlers.

nodes.label: Add / edit a notification target
nodes.detail: Adding and editing share one event. It branches on whether the second argument, notificationID, is present. On failure it returns ok:false and e.message.

nodes.label: Delete a notification target
nodes.detail: Takes a notificationID and runs Notification.delete. After success it re-broadcasts the notification list.

nodes.label: Test send
nodes.detail: Takes the unsaved settings and sends immediately. A failure is written to log.error and answered with ok:false.

nodes.label: Apprise install check
nodes.detail: checkLogin is inside the try, so any exception makes the catch return false unconditionally.

nodes.label: Add a monitor
nodes.detail: Detaches notificationIDList from the monitor before bean.import. The links are created after the save.

nodes.label: Edit a monitor
nodes.detail: After the save, updateMonitorNotification rebuilds the notification links, and a running monitor is restarted.

nodes.label: Login required check
nodes.detail: Throws "You are not logged in." when socket.userID is missing. The shared guard in front of every handler.

nodes.label: Save the notification target
nodes.detail: With an ID it fetches the one row matching id and user_id, otherwise "notification not found". The whole configuration is stored as JSON in config.

nodes.label: Delete the notification target
nodes.detail: Fetches by id and user_id and calls R.trash. Throws "notification not found" if there is no match.

nodes.label: Dispatch to the provider
nodes.detail: If providerList[type] is missing: "Notification type is not supported". Otherwise it calls that provider's send.

nodes.label: Is the apprise command there?
nodes.detail: Returns the result of commandExists("apprise") as is. It checks neither the version nor whether it can actually run.

nodes.label: Apply to every monitor at once
nodes.detail: Walks all of the user's monitors and inserts into monitor_notification only the pairs that are not there yet.

nodes.label: Initialize the provider list
nodes.detail: At startup it registers about a hundred providers keyed by name. A missing or duplicate name throws at startup.

nodes.label: Broadcast the notification list
nodes.detail: Fetches by user_id, turns isDefault/active back into booleans and emits notificationList to every connection of that user.

nodes.label: Rebuild the links
nodes.detail: DELETEs every monitor_notification row for the monitor, then re-INSERTs only the IDs marked true.

nodes.label: Start monitoring
nodes.detail: Starts the beat loop. Notification targets are read from the DB on every beat, so they are not frozen at start time.

nodes.label: Compose the down / recovery notification
nodes.detail: Runs only when !isFirstBeat or the status is DOWN. The message is [name][🔴 Down / ✅ Up] reason. It adds the timezone and other details and sends to each target in turn.

nodes.label: Get the monitor's notification targets
nodes.detail: Joins monitor_notification with notification and returns only the targets linked to that monitor.

nodes.label: Is this beat worth notifying?
nodes.detail: True only for the first beat, UP to DOWN, DOWN to UP, PENDING to DOWN and MAINTENANCE to DOWN. Entering and leaving maintenance is not notified.

nodes.label: Certificate expiry notification
nodes.detail: Sends nothing if notification_sent_history already holds a matching record. If even one send succeeds, it INSERTs the history row.

nodes.label: Store the TLS info and check the expiry
nodes.detail: After saving the TLS info it moves on to the expiry check only when ignoreTls is off and certificate expiry notices are enabled.

nodes.label: Work out the days left on the certificate
nodes.detail: Returns immediately when there are no targets. For each tlsExpiryNotifyDays value (7/14/21 by default) it walks the certificate chain, skipping known roots.

nodes.label: Reshape a send error and rethrow it
nodes.detail: Throws an Error whose message is one line concatenating error.code, the HTTP status and the response body.

nodes.label: Render the message template
nodes.detail: Uses Liquid to interpolate msg / monitorJSON / heartbeatJSON. In a test send, monitorJSON is null.

nodes.label: Send to Telegram
nodes.detail: POSTs sendMessage. With a template it escapes for MarkdownV2, and in a test it fills in dummy values.

nodes.label: Send to a webhook
nodes.detail: GET puts it in the query; POST sends JSON, form-data or a custom body. If the additional-headers JSON is broken it throws before sending.

nodes.label: Send an email
nodes.detail: Sends through nodemailer. The subject and body are only template-rendered when they are customized. Malformed additional headers throw.

nodes.label: Send through Apprise
nodes.detail: Spawns the apprise command. If stdout contains ERROR it throws; if the output is empty it returns "No output from apprise".

nodes.label: One monitoring beat
nodes.detail: Decides the state and builds the heartbeat. An important beat goes to the notification decision, anything else to the resend counter.

nodes.label: Schedule the next beat
nodes.detail: Schedules the next run only after the whole pass, including sending notifications, has finished. A slow target delays the entire beat.

nodes.label: Consecutive DOWN counter
nodes.detail: Incremented on a non-important beat while DOWN. At or above resendInterval it resends, then goes back to 0.

nodes.label: notification table
nodes.detail: name / user_id / is_default / config. config holds the entire form input as JSON (tokens and passwords in plaintext too).

nodes.label: Monitor-to-notification link
nodes.detail: The join table of monitor_id and notification_id. Both sides are ON DELETE CASCADE.

nodes.label: Notification send history
nodes.detail: type / monitor_id / days. Used to stop duplicate certificate expiry notices.

nodes.label: monitor table
nodes.detail: Holds the monitors per user_id. The bulk apply narrows by user_id and walks every row.

nodes.label: Beat history table
nodes.detail: The recovery notification looks up the most recent DOWN with important=1 and passes it into the message as lastDownTime.

nodes.label: setting table
nodes.detail: Holds tlsExpiryNotifyDays. If it is unset or not an array, [7,14,21] is written back.

nodes.label: Telegram Bot API
nodes.detail: /bot<token>/sendMessage on https://api.telegram.org by default. A self-hosted server URL can be set instead.

nodes.label: Webhook destination URL
nodes.detail: Any URL the user enters. It goes through the proxy if one is configured. The response body is never validated.

nodes.label: SMTP server
nodes.detail: Connects with host/port/secure and the credentials. With STARTTLS off it sends unencrypted, which logs a warning.

nodes.label: apprise command
nodes.detail: The apprise installed on the server, launched as an external process. Without it, nothing can be sent.

flows.title: Add a notification target
flows.trigger: Pressing the "Setup Notification" button under Settings > Notifications

steps.label: Return a failure if not logged in
Return ok and the new ID

notes: There is no validation on the server. The name is required only by the dialog's required attribute, and the type is never checked for validity
The whole form input is JSON-encoded into the config column. API tokens and SMTP passwords are stored in plaintext too
The added event is emitted only for a new target, never on an edit

flows.title: Edit a notification target
flows.trigger: Pressing the Edit link in the list under Settings > Notifications

steps.label: Restore the config and show it
Fetch one row by id and user_id
Someone else's ID gives not found

notes: Adding and editing share the addNotification event. Only the presence of the ID in the second argument changes what happens
An edit does not emit added, so editing from the monitor screen leaves the links unchanged
Some installs from older versions have applyExisting baked into the DB, so show() resets it to false every time

flows.title: Send a test notification
flows.trigger: Pressing the "Test" button in the notification dialog

steps.label: Call the implementation for that type
Rendered only when a template is used
Show the result in a toast

notes: The test sends the unsaved form values as they are and writes nothing to the DB
monitorJSON and heartbeatJSON are null, so the body differs from a real notification. Telegram fills in dummy values for MarkdownV2
SMTP has a special case: it only renders the custom subject and body when msg ends with "Testing"

flows.title: Delete the notification target
flows.trigger: Pressing the "Delete" button in the notification dialog

steps.label: Close the settings and show the confirmation

notes: monitor_notification has ON DELETE CASCADE on notification_id, so the links disappear on their own
There is no warning about which monitors use it. Even one in active use is deleted silently
The confirm dialog appears after the settings modal closes. Cancelling does not bring the settings modal back

flows.title: Apply a new notification target to every existing monitor
flows.trigger: Turning on "Apply on all existing monitors" in the notification dialog and saving

steps.label: Save with applyExisting forced to false
Fetch all of the user's monitor IDs
INSERT only the pairs that are missing

notes: applyExisting is reset to false just before saving, so it never lands in the DB. It is a one-shot action that has no effect on the next save
Existing links are never removed, only added. Undoing it means unchecking the box on each monitor
Monitoring is not restarted, but the notification targets are read from the DB on every beat, so the next beat picks it up
This is not the same as "Default enabled" (isDefault). isDefault only pre-checks the box on the new-monitor screen

flows.title: Link a notification target to a monitor
flows.trigger: Ticking a notification target on the monitor edit screen and saving

steps.label: Add a notification target on the spot
On a new monitor the default targets start checked
An edit goes through the same function
DELETE everything, then INSERT the ones set to true

notes: The links are rebuilt every time: delete everything, then recreate. Editing the same monitor from two screens at once means last write wins
notificationIDList is an object of {id: true/false}, and keys set to false are never INSERTed
Editing an existing notification target from the monitor screen does not fire added, so the checkboxes stay as they were

flows.title: A notification goes out when something breaks
flows.trigger: A monitoring beat turned from UP to DOWN

steps.label: Entering maintenance and the like: nothing sent, move on
Important, so on to the notification
JOIN the notification targets through the links
Send to each target in turn
Call the implementation for that type
Every target sent, schedule the next run

notes: Targets are sent to sequentially, awaited in a for loop. Many or slow targets stretch out the whole beat
The body is fixed as [monitor name] [🔴 Down] reason. Formatting is left to each provider's template
Even the first beat notifies when it is DOWN (!isFirstBeat || status===DOWN), so a monitor added while the target is down alerts immediately
The transition into maintenance (UP to MAINTENANCE) is not notified, but maintenance to DOWN is

flows.title: A notification goes out on recovery
flows.trigger: A monitoring beat turned from DOWN to UP

steps.label: Look up the most recent important DOWN
A failure is swallowed and it carries on
JOIN the notification targets through the links

notes: A recovery notification is never sent on isFirstBeat. A monitor that comes up right after being added stays quiet
lastDownTime looks at the transition beat with important=1, not the most recent DOWN beat, so it is when the outage began
If working out the downtime fails it only writes a debug log; the notification still goes out

flows.title: Keep notifying while it stays down
flows.trigger: It stayed DOWN for resendInterval more beats

steps.label: Set the resend count (0 disables it)
Not important, so on to the counter
Below the count: nothing sent, move on
The count is reached, so resend
JOIN the notification targets through the links
Call the implementation for that type
Reset the counter to 0 and schedule the next run

notes: resendInterval is a count of beats, not a duration. Changing interval changes the real-world resend spacing too
An important beat, where the state changed, resets downCount to 0
The resent body is identical to the first one, so the recipient cannot tell it is a resend

flows.title: A notification fails to send
flows.trigger: The target is down, the token has expired, or the send fails for some other reason

steps.label: Call the implementation for that type
An HTTP error or a failed connection
Log it and move to the next target
A failure does not stop the monitoring

notes: A failed send only shows up in the server log. Nothing appears on screen, so the only time a failure is visible is a test send
There is no automatic retry. The one failed message is simply lost, and nothing arrives until the next state change
One failing target is absorbed by try/catch and the remaining targets are still sent to
Webhook and SMTP throw before sending if the additional-headers JSON is broken (nothing reaches the target at all)

flows.title: Warn before the certificate expires
flows.trigger: A beat of an HTTPS monitor picked up TLS info

steps.label: Nothing happens if expiry notices are off
Get the targets (stop if there are none)
Get the threshold days (7/14/21 by default)
Notify for every certificate at or below a threshold
Already sent, so nothing goes out
Send with the days remaining in the body
Call the implementation for that type
Record the history if at least one send succeeded
No history is written when every target failed

notes: If every target fails, no history is written, so the next beat tries again (which makes duplicates unlikely after a recovery)
The walk up a chain stops as soon as it reaches a known root certificate. Intermediates are all inspected by following issuerCertificate
The history check is days <= targetDays, so once a shorter threshold has sent, a longer one never will
If tlsExpiryNotifyDays is unset or not an array, [7,14,21] is written back to the DB on the spot

flows.title: Check whether Apprise is installed
flows.trigger: Choosing Apprise as the notification type and rendering its form

steps.label: Any exception means an unconditional false
The actual send is done by spawn
ERROR in the output means failure

notes: checkApprise also returns false from the catch when the user is not logged in, so "not installed" and "not authenticated" look identical on screen
All it checks is that the command exists. It looks at neither the execute permission nor the version
The send result is judged by string-matching stdout. Empty output returns "No output from apprise" as a success
